chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The greedy one is in the shackles of disgrace.

key_terms.الطَّامِعُ: The greedy one; one who eagerly desires more than enough

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of greed according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this concise aphorism from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies the greedy individual (al-ṭāmiʿ) as one who voluntarily binds himself with the 'shackles of disgrace' (withāq al-dhull). This metaphor underscores the Shia ethical view that greed is not merely a lack of contentment but an active enslavement to worldly desires, resulting in both spiritual degradation and social humiliation. The phrase reflects the broader tradition of linking inner moral states to tangible external consequences, a hallmark of Imam Ali's rhetorical style.
